title: Implement hybrid system model and iterative solver
action: Implement the coupled energy-balance equations for the parabolic dish collector (PDC), thermionic generator (TIG), and thermoelectric device (TEG+TEC) as described in the paper. Use geometric and material parameters: aperture area 12.5 m², receiver area 0.0069 m², cavity wall area 0.0645 m², concentration ratio 1800; cathode work function 1 eV, TIG voltage 0.2 V, TIG plate area 1.6e-2 m²; optical efficiency 0.95; ambient temperature 25 °C, cavity wall temperature 827 °C; thermoelectric module thermal conductivity 61.3 W/K, inter-device heat conductivity 60 W/K; ratio of resistances R2/R=1. Obtain the TD model coefficients (Seebeck coefficient α, figure of merit Z, internal resistance R) from the public reference DOI 10.1016/j.seta.2019.100550. Implement an iterative procedure to solve the coupled nonlinear system (energy balance at TIG cathode, anode, and TEG cold end) for the unknown temperatures Tc, Ta, T2. The solver must converge to a self-consistent temperature set. Write a convergence log to convergence_log.txt (optional).
description: This process step builds the core numerical model of the hybrid system; it is required before any simulation can be run.

title: Solar irradiance sweep and output power curves
action: Using the model and solver from step 1, sweep the incident solar irradiance density I0 over the range from 0 to 3×10^6 W/m² (use at least 50 points to resolve the peak). For each I0, compute the three power quantities: thermionic generator power P_TIG (W), thermoelectric device power P_TD (W), and total hybrid power P_total = P_TIG + P_TD (W). Save the results to power_vs_irradiance.csv.
description: CSV file with one row per irradiance value, containing the computed powers.
output_schema: CSV with header: I0,P_TIG,P_TD,P_total. I0: float, solar irradiance in W/m². P_TIG, P_TD, P_total: float, power in W.
